title: What is the Annual Integrated Economic Survey used for?
gist: The Census Bureau's Annual Integrated Economic Survey (AIES) acts as a benchmark that recalibrates the levels of its faster, smaller-sample monthly and quarterly surveys; summed Monthly Retail Trade Survey sales match the AIES annual total within a few million dollars (about $7.107 trillion in 2024). Since 2023 the AIES has replaced seven annual business surveys with one sent to ~359,000 companies, and FRED has added 5,582 AIES series covering 1,046 activities across seven industries.

insights.claim: The Census Bureau's monthly and quarterly business surveys are built for speed, using smaller samples that are best at measuring period-to-period change, while the Annual Integrated Economic Survey uses a much larger, more detailed sample to recalibrate the levels of those faster series.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Treat monthly Census releases as reliable for direction of change but provisional on levels until the annual benchmark arrives.
insights.quote: Monthly and quarterly Census surveys are built for speed: They use smaller samples and are best at measuring change from one period to the next.
insights.locator: How does the annual survey sharpen

insights.claim: When new Annual Integrated Economic Survey results arrive, the Census Bureau's faster monthly and quarterly series are revised so that their levels match the annual benchmark.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Annual benchmark release dates are a known source of level revisions to monthly macro series such as retail sales.
insights.quote: when new annual results arrive, the faster series are revised to match it
insights.locator: How does the annual survey sharpen

insights.claim: Adding up the 12 Monthly Retail Trade Survey values for any year reproduces the Annual Integrated Economic Survey retail sales total within a few million dollars; in 2024 both came to about $7.107 trillion.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: After benchmarking, monthly retail sales are consistent with the annual census-style total, so annualized monthly data can be used for level analysis once revised.
insights.quote: In 2024, the latest full-year data available at the time of this writing, both came to about $7.107 trillion.

insights.claim: The Annual Integrated Economic Survey also updates the Census Business Register, the master list from which other Census economic surveys draw their samples, so it shapes the sampling frame of the high-frequency surveys as well as their levels.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Quality of the annual survey propagates into every downstream Census business survey via the sample frame.
insights.quote: The AIES also updates the Census Business Register, the master list from which other economic surveys draw their samples.
insights.locator: How does the annual survey sharpen

insights.claim: Other U.S. statistical agencies use the same benchmarking approach: the Bureau of Economic Analysis to derive industry output for GDP, the Bureau of Labor Statistics for the producer price index and productivity measures, and the Federal Reserve Board for its index of industrial production.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: GDP industry output, PPI, productivity and industrial production are all exposed to annual benchmark revisions, so early prints should be treated as provisional.
insights.locator: Other statistical agencies perform similar adjustments.

themes.theme: Scope and history of the AIES

insights.claim: Starting in 2023, the Census Bureau's Annual Integrated Economic Survey replaced seven separate annual business surveys with a single survey sent to approximately 359,000 companies.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: The consolidated survey creates one consistent annual benchmark across sectors, though 2023 marks a methodological break to keep in mind.
insights.quote: Starting in 2023, the AIES replaced seven separate annual business surveys with one, which is sent to approximately 359,000 companies.

insights.claim: FRED recently added 5,582 Annual Integrated Economic Survey series covering revenues, expenses, payroll and employment for 1,046 economic activities across seven industries: agriculture, construction, manufacturing, mining, retail, services and wholesale trade.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: A large new free dataset for industry-level analysis of revenues, costs and labor is now available in FRED.
insights.quote: FRED recently added 5,582 series from the AIES.

insights.claim: Many Annual Integrated Economic Survey series in FRED extend well before 2023 because the Census folded in results from the legacy surveys: retail and wholesale back to 1992, manufacturing to 2007, and services to 2013.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: History length varies by sector, limiting long-run comparisons for services versus retail and wholesale.
insights.quote: retail and wholesale to 1992, manufacturing to 2007, and services to 2013
